html:
The last major outbreak of bubonic plague in western Europe, which struck the French port of Marseille in 1720 and spread through Provence until 1722.

It arrived on the Grand Saint Antoine, a merchant ship from the eastern Mediterranean carrying cloth. Several people on board had died of plague, but the city's merchants wanted the cargo for a fair, and the quarantine was cut short. Within weeks the disease was loose in the old town.

Deaths ran to around a thousand a day at the worst. Bodies piled in the streets until convicts from the galleys were ordered to clear them. About half of the city's roughly 90,000 people died, and around 100,000 across the region. To stop it spreading, the authorities built a stone wall across the hills of Provence, guarded by soldiers.

Plague had haunted Europe since the Black Death. After Marseille, stricter quarantines in Mediterranean ports and other changes helped keep it out of western Europe. Later outbreaks such as the plague in Hong Kong struck elsewhere.
sum: The last major outbreak of bubonic plague in western Europe, which struck the French port of Marseille in 1720 and spread through Provence until 1722.
